meta.subtitle: Margins are expanding on a consignment-heavy mix, but the price already carries much of it; HOLD

analystCommentary: Liquidity Services delivered a clean fiscal third quarter (ended June 30, 2026): the earnings release shows GMV of $453.0 million, up 10%, revenue of $129.6 million, up 8%, and Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA of $22.0 million, up 30%. Profit is growing faster than volume because more of the business runs through consignment, where the company earns a fee rather than reselling inventory. The balance sheet carries $231.1 million of cash with zero financial debt. The problem is price, not quality. At $43.23 the stock sits close to its 52-week high of $45.00 and trades on 42.4x trailing earnings, while the two covering analysts' targets span only $50.00–$52.00. Our scenarios produce a probability-weighted value modestly above the current price with a real downside if volume growth or retail supply falters, which supports a HOLD rather than a BUY.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Liquidity Services runs online marketplaces where government agencies and companies sell surplus, returned and used assets. The 10-Q MD&A describes three reportable segments: GovDeals (public-sector surplus and real estate), Retail Supply Chain Group or RSCG (returned and overstocked consumer goods, sold mainly on Liquidation.com and through direct-to-consumer channels), and Capital Assets Group or CAG (industrial and heavy equipment). Machinio, an equipment search engine with seller software, and Software Solutions are combined and reported as Machinio & Software Solutions. The financial data in this report treats the company as a single consolidated unit. Revenue comes from two models. Under the purchase model the company buys inventory and books the full sale price; under the consignment model it books only its commission. The MD&A says consignment was 83.1% of consolidated GMV in the quarter ended June 30, 2026. The fiscal year ends September 30, so the quarter the data vendor labels Q2'26 is the company's fiscal third quarter.

thesis.body: The business is getting more profitable per dollar of volume. In the fiscal third quarter, GAAP net income rose 41% on revenue growth of 8%, and the release attributes the margin gain to asset-light consignment growth and operating leverage. Cash of $231.1 million with no financial debt leaves room for buybacks and acquisitions. Against that, the market already prices much of the improvement: the stock trades near the top of its 52-week range and above the forward multiples a slower-growing marketplace would usually earn. Growth in auction participants turned negative in the quarter, and the RSCG segment depends partly on inventory bought from Amazon. We rate the shares HOLD with a target range of $44 to $52.

catalysts: Fiscal fourth-quarter results against guidance that calls for GMV of $415 to $455 million; see Growth.
Further gains in RSCG direct profit from the consignment and sell-in-place programs discussed under Financials.
Progress toward management's $2 Billion annual GMV target, set out under Growth.
Use of the cash balance for buybacks or acquisitions; see Management.
risks: Falling auction participation could slow GMV; see Risks.
The 10-K flags dependence on Amazon.com, Inc. as an RSCG inventory vendor; see Risks.
The full use of the federal NOL in FY25 raises cash taxes in FY26; see Financials.
Valuation leaves limited room for a miss; see Valuation.

financials.incomeCommentary: Revenue grew {+ +31.2% +} in FY25 to $476.7M, ahead of the growth rates of FY22 through FY24. Gross margin moved the other way, to 43.8% in FY25 from 58.2% in FY21. A lower gross margin is not by itself a warning sign here: the filings do not explain the full five-year decline, but a purchase-model sale books the whole price as revenue while a consignment sale books only the fee, so mix moves the ratio. Operating margin is the better gauge. It was 7.4% in FY25 and 9.0% on a trailing-twelve-month basis, and the quarter ended June 30, 2026 printed 10.9%. In that quarter, the earnings release shows RSCG segment direct profit and Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA each growing several times faster than revenue. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.32 against Non-GAAP Adjusted Diluted EPS of $0.45; the gap is mostly stock compensation, which the reconciliation shows rising year over year, so adjusted figures flatter the earnings that accrue to shareholders. The tax line is the main headwind. The release says the federal net operating loss carryforward was fully used during FY25 and guides to an FY26 effective tax rate of approximately 30% to 34%, so cash taxes rise in FY26. Our view: margins are improving for real, but the growth in GAAP earnings is not as fast as the adjusted figures suggest.
financials.balanceCommentary: The balance sheet is a strength. The earnings release reports cash balances of $231.1 million at June 30, 2026, made up of $219.8 million of cash and cash equivalents and $11.3 million of short-term investments, with zero financial debt. The vendor's debt and cash rows are blank, so we rely on the release for those figures. The current ratio was 1.58 on a trailing basis, up from 1.21 in FY21. One caution: much of the cash in a marketplace operator can relate to buyer proceeds owed to sellers, and the excerpts do not split how much is truly free. We therefore treat the cash as a cushion and a source of optionality, not as a figure to subtract in full from the market value.
financials.cashflowCommentary: Free cash flow was $59M in FY25, a margin of 12.4%, below the 16.9% of FY24 and the 23.3% of FY21. Capital needs are light; the vendor rounds annual capital expenditure to zero in billions throughout the five-year table. The release cites strong free cash flow in the fiscal third quarter but gives no figure in the excerpt. The counter-case is that cash conversion has trended down even as revenue grew, and higher cash taxes in FY26 will weigh on it further. We expect free cash flow to keep funding buybacks, but not to rise as fast as adjusted EBITDA.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: The shares trade on 42.4x trailing earnings, 23.2x trailing EV/EBITDA and 2.8x sales. On a forward basis the multiple is 26.2x next-twelve-month earnings and ~23.5x FY27E. Consensus EPS is $1.65 for FY26E and $1.84 for FY27E. The vendor does not state whether those estimates are GAAP or adjusted; because GAAP and adjusted EPS diverged in the fiscal third quarter, the forward multiples should not be read as GAAP-based. The vendor's consensus revenue line for FY26E and FY27E is not usable. Two analysts cover the stock, both at Buy, with a consensus target of $51.00 and a range of $50.00–$52.00. That is thin coverage and a narrow range, so it adds little independent evidence. The trailing multiple is high because FY25 GAAP EPS of $0.87 still reflects lower margins; the forward multiples are more reasonable but already assume consensus earnings growth is delivered. Our view is that the stock is fairly priced to modestly cheap if consensus is met, with little cushion if it is not.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: The fiscal fourth quarter lands at the top of guidance, RSCG keeps shifting to consignment and direct-to-consumer, and GMV growth holds near the 10% of the fiscal third quarter as the company moves toward its $2 Billion target. The market pays above the top of the $50.00–$52.00 Street range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Earnings track consensus, with FY27E EPS of $1.84, and the stock holds its current 26.2x next-twelve-month multiple as the estimate rolls forward. Margin gains continue but higher cash taxes slow GAAP earnings growth.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Either RSCG loses Amazon inventory on acceptable terms, or falling auction participation drags GMV growth toward zero. Either one would break the margin story and push the stock toward the middle of its $21.67 – $45.00 52-week range.

valuation.scenarioCommentary: We put 50% on the Base case at $48, which simply holds today's forward multiple on rising consensus earnings and sits just under the Street target. The Bull case at $57 and the Bear case at $34 each get 25%. We weight the Bear as high as the Bull because it needs only one of two independent shocks, either a change in the Amazon supply relationship or a stall in buyer activity, while the Bull needs several things to go right at once. The resulting probability-weighted value sits above the current price, but by less than the size of the Bear drawdown, so the reward does not compensate for the risk enough to justify a BUY. The target range of $44 to $52 brackets the Base case.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: The financial data treats the company as one unit, and FY25 revenue of $476.7M is shown as a single consolidated total. The 10-Q, however, reports three segments (GovDeals, RSCG and CAG) plus Machinio & Software Solutions. The earnings release shows that the segments behave very differently. In the fiscal third quarter GovDeals GMV rose 9%, RSCG GMV rose 19%, and CAG GMV fell 1% on project timing. GovDeals and the Machinio businesses earn mostly fees, so almost all their revenue converts to segment direct profit. RSCG carries the purchase-model inventory and converts far less of its revenue to direct profit, which is why its shift toward consignment matters so much for the consolidated margin.

moatFactors.name: Buyer network
moatFactors.body: The MD&A reports 6.4 million registered buyers at June 30, 2026, up from 5.9 million twelve months earlier. More buyers should mean better prices for sellers, which in turn attracts more supply. The counter-case is that registrations are not activity: the release shows auction participants fell 5% in the fiscal third quarter even as completed transactions rose 17%.

moatFactors.name: Public-sector seller base
moatFactors.body: GovDeals serves city, county, state and federal agencies in the United States and Canada, per the MD&A. These sellers tend to stay once their disposal processes run through a platform, and the segment's fee model converts nearly all its revenue to segment direct profit. The limit is that real estate auctions within GovDeals can be postponed or cancelled, which the release flags as a source of variability.

moatFactors.name: Asset-light consignment model
moatFactors.body: Consignment was 83.1% of consolidated GMV in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, against 82.5% a year earlier, according to the MD&A. Fee-based sales carry no inventory risk and lift direct-profit margins. This is an operating advantage rather than a barrier; a rival could offer the same terms.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. The buyer base and government relationships give the company an advantage that should persist for years, and the shift to consignment improves the economics. It is not WIDE because the 10-K describes the markets as intensely competitive, the RSCG segment relies in part on a single large vendor, and buyer participation fell in the latest quarter. The advantage looks durable in GovDeals and less certain in RSCG and CAG.

points: Management guides fiscal fourth-quarter GMV of $415 to $455 million and GAAP diluted EPS of $0.30 to $0.39. The release expects RSCG GMV and revenue to fall sequentially while direct profit stays strong, so the quarter should be judged on profit, not volume.

The CEO's statement in the release refers to a $2 Billion annual GMV target. The proxy shows FY25 GMV of $1.571 billion. The release gives no date for reaching the target, so we treat it as direction rather than a forecast.

Completed transactions rose 17% in the fiscal third quarter while auction participants fell 5%, per the release. More sales from fewer bidders can reflect better matching, but it can also mean the buyer pool is thinning; the release does not explain the decline.

The MD&A lists industry trends it believes support long-term growth, including more returned merchandise from online retail and more outsourcing of surplus disposal. These are management's views, not measured figures.

CAG revenue rose 18% in the quarter on improved take-rates on multinational projects even as its GMV fell, and the outlook cites a strong pipeline of international project-based work. Project timing makes this segment the least predictable contributor.

management.leadership: Bill Angrick is Chairman and CEO, per the DEF 14A dated January 16, 2026; the proxy does not give tenure in the excerpt. The other named executive officers for fiscal 2025 are Jorge A. Celaya (Chief Financial Officer), John P. Daunt (Chief Commercial Officer), Steven J. Weiskircher (Chief Technology Officer) and Mark A. Shaffer (Chief Legal Officer and Corporate Secretary). Execution in the fiscal third quarter was strong on profit, with Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA up 30% per the release. The weak spot is the decline in auction participants, which management did not address in the release excerpt.
management.capitalAllocation: The company carries no financial debt and pays no dividend. The release says $15.0 million of repurchase authorization remained at June 30, 2026, and the vendor shows FY25 share repurchases of $16.2M in its highlight data. Diluted weighted shares are expected to be approximately 33.0 million in the fiscal fourth quarter. Stock compensation is rising, per the reconciliation, so buybacks partly offset dilution rather than shrinking the share count. The 10-K lists acquisitions as a risk if integration falls short, and the MD&A refers to an acquisition in GovDeals without detail in the excerpt. Our view: the balance sheet supports more buybacks, but the remaining authorization is small relative to the cash, and the excerpts do not show a stated plan for the rest.
management.governance: The same proxy says 75% of the board as of that date, are independent under Nasdaq standards. Mr. Angrick holds both the Chairman and CEO roles and is not independent, and a former President and COO who retired in 2009 is not treated as independent despite qualifying. The proxy reports no related-party transactions since the beginning of fiscal 2025. Pay is tilted to performance: 91% of the CEO's targeted total direct compensation for fiscal 2025 was variable, and 50% of NEO stock awards had performance-based vesting. Separately, the 10-K risk factors say provisions of the charter, bylaws and Delaware law inhibit potential acquisition bids. For outside holders, this means a board with an independent majority but a combined Chairman and CEO and defenses that make a takeover premium less likely.
management.insiderOwnership: The proxy excerpt does not include beneficial ownership figures, so we cannot say how much stock the CEO, directors or large holders own. The pay structure ties a large share of executive pay to equity and performance targets, which aligns management with shareholders in part, but without ownership data we cannot judge how far insiders control the vote.

idiosyncratic: Amazon supply. The 10-K risk factors state that if Amazon stopped selling inventory to the company on acceptable terms, or changed the mix and quantity it makes available, the company likely could not find alternative inventory in a timely way. This sits inside RSCG, the segment that drove most of the quarter's profit gain.

Buyer engagement. Auction participants fell 5% in the fiscal third quarter, per the release. If the decline continues, sellers could see weaker recovery and move volume elsewhere; watch participant counts in the fiscal fourth-quarter release.

Purchase-model inventory. The 10-K warns that misjudging the ability to sell assets where the company takes inventory risk can lower margins. Purchase programs in RSCG increased modestly in the quarter, per the release.
Project timing in CAG and real estate timing in GovDeals. The release says both can swing results from quarter to quarter, which makes single-quarter misses likely even if the trend holds.
risks.systemic: The 10-Q MD&A flags tariffs, used-vehicle price volatility, slowing electric-vehicle adoption, inflation and higher borrowing costs as factors that can affect asset supply, buyer demand and transaction timing. It says revenue tied to Russia, Ukraine, Israel, Iran and Venezuela was not material. A surplus marketplace can benefit when companies shed assets in a downturn, but weaker buyer financing and lower used-asset prices would cut the other way; the filing does not say which effect dominates. The stock also trades at a premium multiple, so a broad de-rating in growth stocks would hit it regardless of results.

body: We rate Liquidity Services HOLD with a target range of $44 to $52. The fiscal third quarter confirmed that the shift to consignment is lifting margins, and the debt-free balance sheet limits financial risk. The share price, close to the 52-week high, already reflects that progress.

We would turn more constructive on a pullback toward the low end of our range, or on evidence that auction participation is growing again alongside completed transactions. We would turn more cautious on any sign that Amazon inventory terms are changing or that fiscal fourth-quarter GMV lands below the $415 low end of guidance.
